about.title: A Different Rhythm of Living
about.text1: In the hills of Verduno, within the vineyards of Monvigliero, Scarpa Villas offers a rare way to experience Barolo.
about.text2: Inspired by the philosophy of Scarpa, it goes beyond a place to stay – it is shaped by wine, time, and the land itself.
about.text3: Here, days unfold slowly, between the silence of the vines, the warmth of the sun, and the rituals of Piedmontese life.

experience.paragraph1: Scarpa Villas were created as a natural extension of the Scarpa winery — a place where the philosophy of wine can be lived, not only tasted.
experience.paragraph2: Founded in 1900, Scarpa has always believed that great wine is shaped by time, patience, and a deep connection to the land.
experience.paragraph3: The villas bring guests closer to that philosophy through the vineyards of Monvigliero, the culture of Barolo, and experiences rooted in the traditions of Piedmont.

storyHero.subtitle: A place shaped by time, wine, and people

storyChapters.heading: Scarpa Villas is part of a wider story — one that begins in the <italic1>vineyards of Piedmont</italic1> and continues through wine, people, and a way of life shaped over <italic2>generations</italic2>.

storyVillasCTA.text: Scarpa Villas bring this story to life — offering a way to experience Barolo through space, time, and connection to the land.

originsIntro.titleLine1: In the hills of the Langhe,
originsIntro.titleLine2: time is not measured in years,
originsIntro.textLine1: What exists today is the result of centuries of quiet transformation —
originsIntro.textLine2: a landscape shaped slowly, almost imperceptibly, over time.

originsHistory.topText: Long before Barolo became one of the world's most celebrated wine regions, these hills were already inhabited and cultivated.
originsHistory.bottomText: Over centuries, the Langhe evolved through layered histories — from prehistoric settlement and early agriculture in Piedmont to the Roman presence that further shaped the region through roads, farming, and viticulture.

originsMedieval.titleLine1: In the Middle Ages, the villages that define the
originsMedieval.titleLine2: region today began to take form, and the vineyard
originsMedieval.titleLine3: landscape continued to develop into what we now
originsMedieval.text: What you see today is not a place that was created at once, but one shaped over time — by generations who lived, worked, and cultivated this land.

originsMonvigliero.text1: Located above the village of Verduno, on the northern edge of the Barolo appellation, these vineyards have long been known for their distinctive character — refined, expressive, and deeply connected to the identity of the region.
originsMonvigliero.text2Bold: one of the most distinctive crus of Barolo
originsMonvigliero.text2End: , shaped by its altitude, exposure, and the quiet balance between sun and air that defines these hills.
originsMonvigliero.text3End: grow side by side, continuing a tradition that reflects both the depth and the quiet elegance of this place.

originsCTA.title: SCARPA VILLAS CONTINUE THIS STORY
originsCTA.textLine1: CONTEMPORARY IN COMFORT, YET ROOTED IN A LANDSCAPE
originsCTA.textLine2: THAT HAS EVOLVED OVER CENTURIES, THEY OFFER A WAY TO EXPERIENCE BAROLO
originsCTA.textLine3: NOT AS A VISITOR, BUT AS PART OF ITS ONGOING RHYTHM.

scarpaWineryIntro.title:
For over a century, Scarpa has been sharing wines
that reflect time, place, and patience
scarpaWineryIntro.textLine1: Rooted in Piedmont, its philosophy goes beyond production —
scarpaWineryIntro.textLine2: it is a way of understanding wine.

scarpaWineryLove.title: Wine For Love
scarpaWineryLove.paragraph1: Scarpa was founded in 1900 by Antonio Scarpa, who moved from Venice to Nizza Monferrato in search of opportunity — and found something more.
scarpaWineryLove.paragraph2: Two connections made him stay: the untapped potential of the land, and his love for Ernestina Ottavia Deantonio, who became his wife in 1908.
scarpaWineryLove.paragraph3: Together, they built a winery with a clear ambition — to reveal the true potential of Piedmontese wines, starting with Barbera, at a time when it was still underestimated.

scarpaWineryEvolution.title: Evolution
scarpaWineryEvolution.leftText: Over the decades, Scarpa evolved through a succession of visionaries — from Antonio Scarpa to Mario Pesce, Carlo Castino, and Silvio Pinchera.
scarpaWineryEvolution.rightText: Each brought a deeper understanding of the land, refining a style built on elegance, longevity, and respect for the vineyard.

scarpaWineryProcess.title: Time, Purity, And Patience
scarpaWineryProcess.paragraph1: Scarpa wines are not forced — they are allowed to evolve.
scarpaWineryProcess.paragraph2: Long aging, minimal intervention, and a deep respect for native grape varieties define a style rooted in purity and expression.
scarpaWineryProcess.paragraph3: Each decision, from vineyard to cellar, is guided by a simple belief: great wine reveals itself over time.

scarpaWineryVineyards.title: Vineyards
scarpaWineryVineyards.paragraph1: Scarpa cultivates vineyards across Monferrato and Langhe, combining historic estates with carefully selected crus.
scarpaWineryVineyards.paragraph2: From the single-body vineyard of Poderi Bricchi to the hills of Barolo and Barbaresco — including Monvigliero in Verduno — each site contributes to a broader understanding of Piedmont's identity.

scarpaWineryCellar.title: Cellar
scarpaWineryCellar.paragraph1: In the historic cellars of Nizza Monferrato, wine follows its own rhythm.
scarpaWineryCellar.paragraph2: Large barrels, long aging, and time itself shape wines designed not only for the present, but for decades to come.

scarpaWineryVillas.title: Villas
scarpaWineryVillas.paragraph1: Scarpa Villas extend this philosophy beyond the glass.
scarpaWineryVillas.paragraph2: Set among the vineyards, they offer a way to experience the same values — time, space, and connection to the land — through living, not just tasting.

articles.title: Monaco Life
articles.text: Just over two and a half hours from Monaco, the rolling vineyards of Italy’s Langhe unfold across the hills of Piedmont, home to some of the world’s most celebrated wines and one of the country’s great gastronomic regions.

articles.title: Gala
articles.text: The hills of Piedmont still hide a few well-kept treasures. Nestled in the heart of the Barolo vineyards, Scarpa Villas offers an immersive experience of the Italian art of living, with exceptional wine tastings, leisurely gourmet meals, and scenic bike rides.

articles.title: Times Monaco
articles.text: Scarpa Villas are not simply a luxury destination. They are an invitation to experience Piedmont at its very best through its landscapes, its people, its traditions, and its wines.

regionHero.title: The Region
regionHero.subtitle: Discover the Langhe beyond the villas

regionIntro.titleLine1: A landscape shaped by vineyards, villages,
regionIntro.titleLine2: and traditions — where every road leads
regionIntro.paragraph1: Piedmont is a region in the north of Italy defined by contrast — between mountains and rolling hills, between cities and countryside, between history and a way of life that has remained deeply rooted in the land.
regionIntro.paragraph2: Within it lies the Langhe — a UNESCO-listed landscape shaped over centuries by vineyards, small villages, and agricultural traditions. This is where Barolo and Barbaresco are born, but the region is more than its wines.

top.titleLine1: The Langhe is not organised around
top.paragraph1: Distances are short, but the experience unfolds slowly — through winding roads, changing light, and places that reveal themselves gradually.
top.paragraph2: To understand the Langhe is not to see everything, but to move through it in the right way.

bottom.paragraph1: Some follow the villages and their history, others the vineyards and their landscapes, others the traditions of food and local life.
bottom.paragraph2Line1: What defines the experience is not the destination,
bottom.paragraph2Line2: but the way these elements come together.

regionWineLandscape.title: Wine & Landscape
regionWineLandscape.paragraph1: The Langhe is shaped by vineyards — not as scenery, but as a living system that defines the identity of the region.
regionWineLandscape.paragraph2: From panoramic viewpoints like La Morra Belvedere to the quiet roads around Verduno and Monvigliero, the landscape is something you move through, not simply observe.
regionWineLandscape.paragraph3: Rows of vines follow the contours of the hills, changing with the seasons — from the green of spring to the deep tones of autumn.

vineyardRoads.title: Scenic Vineyard Roads
vineyardRoads.subtitle: Winding roads between Verduno and Barolo, where the landscape reveals itself gradually.

laMorra.title: La Morra Belvedere
laMorra.subtitle: The most iconic panoramic view in the Langhe.

cappella.title: Cappella delle Brunate
cappella.subtitle: A small chapel transformed into a contemporary artwork by Sol LeWitt and David Tremlett.

cedro.title: Il Cedro del Libano
cedro.subtitle: A solitary tree over 160 years old, standing above the vineyards of La Morra — a quiet landmark in the landscape.

regionVillagesHistory.title: Villages & History
regionVillagesHistory.paragraph1:
The villages of the Langhe define its structure —
Barolo, Serralunga d’Alba, Verduno, La Morra.
regionVillagesHistory.paragraph2: Many of them took shape in the Middle Ages, when castles, agricultural systems, and early wine production began to organise the landscape.
regionVillagesHistory.paragraph3:
Today, they remain small and unchanged in scale, each offering
a different perspective on the region — from fortified hilltop towns
to quiet residential villages.
regionVillagesHistory.paragraph4: Walking through them is less about sightseeing, and more about understanding how the region has evolved over time.

cherasco.title: Cherasco
cherasco.subtitle: A refined town of wide streets and baroque architecture — known for antiques, chocolate, and a slower pace.

barolo.title: Barolo
barolo.subtitle: The historic center of the wine region, with the Wine Museum and castle.

serralunga.title: Serralunga d’Alba
serralunga.subtitle: A medieval fortress rising above the vineyards.

grinzane.title: Grinzane Cavour
grinzane.subtitle: A UNESCO-listed castle and home to one of the region’s oldest enotecas.

monforte.title: Monforte d’Alba
monforte.subtitle: Known for its open-air amphitheatre, where concerts take place during summer evenings.

regionFoodTraditions.title: Food & Traditions
regionFoodTraditions.paragraph1:
Food in the Langhe is not an attraction — it is part of everyday life.
From the white truffle of Alba to local dishes served in small trattorias,
the region’s identity is deeply tied to its culinary traditions.
regionFoodTraditions.paragraph2:
Experiences such as the Merenda Sinoira — a traditional late-afternoon
table of local dishes — reflect a way of eating that is social, generous,
and rooted in the land.
regionFoodTraditions.paragraph3:
Here, gastronomy is not separate from the landscape —
it is a direct expression of it.

hazelnuts.title: Tonda Gentile Hazelnuts
hazelnuts.subtitle: A defining product of the region, grown across the hills beyond the vineyards.

albaMarket.title: Alba Market
albaMarket.subtitle: A Saturday market that reflects the rhythm of local life — farmers, products, and everyday exchange.

whiteTruffle.title: White Truffle Season
whiteTruffle.subtitle: One of the most unique gastronomic experiences in Italy.

merendaSinoira.title: Merenda Sinoira
merendaSinoira.subtitle: A traditional table of local dishes, shared slowly in the afternoon.

regionBeyondRoutes.title: Beyond the Main Routes
regionBeyondRoutes.paragraph1:
Beyond the well-known villages, the Langhe extends
into quieter, less explored areas.
regionBeyondRoutes.paragraph2:
In places like Alta Langa, the landscape becomes wilder,
and the pace even slower.
regionBeyondRoutes.paragraph3:
Here, small producers continue traditions that define the region —
from cheese making to hazelnut cultivation.
regionBeyondRoutes.paragraph4:
These areas reveal another side of Piedmont — less visible,
but equally essential to its identity.

cookiePolicyContent.cookiesWeUseText: Scarpa Villas may use technical cookies that are necessary for the website to function correctly. Where analytics or other non-essential technologies are used, they are managed in accordance with applicable data protection and cookie regulations.

cookiePolicyContent.thirdPartyText: Some features of the website may rely on services provided by third parties. These services may process information according to their own privacy and cookie policies.

privacyPolicyContent.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicyContent.intro: Scarpa Villas respects your privacy and is committed to protecting the personal information you provide when using this website. This Privacy Policy explains what information may be collected, how it is used, and the choices available to you.
privacyPolicyContent.dataText: When you contact Scarpa Villas through the website, we may collect personal information that you voluntarily provide, including your name, email address, telephone number, areas of interest, travel details and any information included in your message.
privacyPolicyContent.purposeText: The information you provide is used to respond to your enquiries, assist with villa selection, provide information about stays and experiences, and communicate with you regarding your request.
privacyPolicyContent.formsText: Personal information submitted through our contact and villa enquiry forms is used solely for handling your request and communicating with you. Please do not include sensitive personal information in free-text message fields unless it is necessary for your enquiry.
privacyPolicyContent.servicesText: Scarpa Villas may use trusted third-party service providers to operate certain website features and process enquiries submitted through the website. These providers may process personal information only as necessary to provide their services.
privacyPolicyContent.retentionText: Personal information is retained only for as long as reasonably necessary to respond to your enquiry, manage our relationship with you, comply with applicable legal obligations, or establish, exercise or defend legal claims.
privacyPolicyContent.rightsText: Subject to applicable data protection law, you may have the right to request access to your personal data, request its correction or deletion, restrict or object to certain processing, request data portability where applicable, and withdraw consent where processing is based on consent.
privacyPolicyContent.securityText: Appropriate technical and organisational measures are used to protect personal information against unauthorised access, loss, misuse, alteration or disclosure.
privacyPolicyContent.thirdPartyText: The Scarpa Villas website may contain links to external websites or services. Scarpa Villas is not responsible for the privacy practices or content of those third-party websites.
privacyPolicyContent.changesText: This Privacy Policy may be updated from time to time to reflect changes to the website, our services or applicable legal requirements.
privacyPolicyContent.contactText: For questions regarding this Privacy Policy or the processing of your personal information, please contact Scarpa Villas at

cookieBanner.text: We use cookies to ensure the proper functioning of our website and improve your browsing experience.
